what_its_for: Tipranavir is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children 2 years and older. It belongs to a class of drugs called protease inhibitors. It works by blocking a protein that HIV needs to make copies of itself, helping to lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keep your immune system stronger. Tipranavir is always used together with another HIV medicine called ritonavir (Norvir) and is typically prescribed when other HIV treatments have not worked well enough.
how_to_take: Always take tipranavir exactly as your doctor or pharmacist tells you. Take it together with ritonavir (Norvir) — do not take tipranavir alone. Tipranavir capsules should be swallowed whole with food to help your body absorb the medicine properly and to reduce stomach upset. If you are taking the oral solution (liquid), shake the bottle gently before each use and measure your dose carefully using the measuring device provided — do not use a regular household spoon. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsules. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as this can make the virus harder to treat.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg (two 250 mg capsules) taken twice a day (every 12 hours), along with 200 mg of ritonavir twice a day. For children aged 2 to 18 years, the dose is based on their weight and is calculated by your doctor. Always follow the exact dosing schedule your doctor has given you. Take your doses as evenly spaced throughout the day as possible.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is within 5 hours of when you were supposed to take it. If more than 5 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one. It may help to set a daily alarm or reminder so you do not forget your doses.
storage: Capsules: Store in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F or 2°C to 8°C) before opening the bottle. Once opened, you may store the capsules at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 60 days. Keep track of when you opened the bottle. Oral solution (liquid): Store at room temperature (59°F to 86°F or 15°C to 30°C). Do not refrigerate the liquid. Use within 60 days of opening the bottle. Write the date you opened the bottle on the label. Keep all forms of this medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep out of reach of children. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking tipranavir with certain other medicines unless your doctor says it is safe, as serious drug interactions can occur. Do not take tipranavir with alfuzosin, amiodarone, certain cholesterol medicines (such as lovastatin or simvastatin), ergot medicines (used for migraines), certain sedatives (like oral midazolam or triazolam), rifampin, St. John's Wort herbal supplement, lurasidone, pimozide, or sildenafil for pulmonary arterial hypertension (Revatio). Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol. Do not take extra vitamin E supplements beyond what is in a standard daily multivitamin, especially while taking the oral solution, as tipranavir liquid already contains vitamin E. Avoid becoming pregnant while on this medicine — talk to your doctor about safe birth control options. Grapefruit and grapefruit juice may affect this medicine, so ask your doctor or pharmacist before consuming them.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or whites of the eyes (jaundice), dark or tea-colored urine, pale stools, severe nausea or vomiting, stomach pain, or unusual tiredness; signs of bleeding in the brain such as sudden severe headache, weakness on one side of the body, confusion, or vision changes; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; high blood sugar symptoms such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision; signs of infection or any new or worsening symptoms; unusual bruising or bleeding; muscle pain or weakness. Also tell your doctor about any new medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements you start taking.
when_it_works: Tipranavir does not cure HIV, but it starts working to lower the amount of HIV in your blood (called your viral load) within the first few weeks of treatment. Most people begin to see improvement in their lab results (CD4 count going up and viral load going down) within the first few months. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day, even when you feel well and have no symptoms, because HIV is still active in your body. Missing doses can allow the virus to grow and become resistant to this and other HIV medicines.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of tipranavir during pregnancy is not fully established. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed if you are HIV-positive or taking tipranavir, as HIV can be passed to your baby through breast milk. Liver disease: Tipranavir may not be right for you if you have moderate to severe liver disease (Child-Pugh B or C). Tell your doctor about any liver problems including hepatitis B or C. Children: Not recommended for children under 2 years of age. Elderly: Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects. Diabetes: Monitor blood sugar closely as tipranavir can raise blood sugar levels. Hemophilia: Tell your doctor if you have a bleeding disorder, as tipranavir may increase the risk of bleeding.
